name: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy
oracle_text:
Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced.
{5}{G}{U}: Look at the top five cards of your library. You may put a non-Human creature card from among them onto the battlefield. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.
blocked_sentences: Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced.

needs.what: A player-wide static in the exact shape of `double_land_mana`, but whose subject is a **nonland** permanent tapped for mana. `double_land_mana` already IS this printed sentence -- `player_statics.player_doubles_land_mana` is docstringed with it word for word ("whenever you tap a land for mana, add one mana of any type that land produced", Zendikar Resurgent) -- and Kinnan is that card with one printed word changed. So the work is to make the permanent class a parameter instead of a hardcoded `is_land`, not to invent a mechanism. Concretely: `costs._sources_of` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:299-302) and `costs.activate_mana_ability` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:1791) each compute `is_land = "Land" in chars(state, oid).types` and then `doubled = is_land and player_doubles_land_mana(...)`; `costs.mana_produced` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:669) takes the resulting bool and scales the produced tuple. A `double_nonland_mana` static read at those same two call sites with `not is_land` would land Kinnan, and generalising the class key (so one static carries a permanent filter -- Kinnan's "nonland permanent", Mana Reflection's "a permanent") would land the neighbours too. It must be read at the mana choke point, never queued: this is a triggered mana ability (605.1b) that resolves immediately and never uses the stack (605.4a), which is the same argument that put `double_land_mana` and `add_mana_on_tap` there. The `mana_produced` simplification already documented in docs/rules-coverage.md (a dual doubles whatever it produced rather than offering a free choice of type, because a mana ability cannot ask) carries over unchanged and is the right trade here too.
needs.why_existing_wont_do:
Three near misses, each wrong in a way that ships a different card.

(1) `double_land_mana` is the right effect on the wrong half of the board. `is_land` is computed inline at both call sites and the static takes no filter at all -- the loader's player-wide statics carry only `affects_player` here -- so there is no spelling of it that reaches a Sol Ring, a Bloom Tender or a Birds of Paradise. Written as `double_land_mana`, Kinnan would double every land and no nonland permanent: the complement of the printed line.

(2) `add_mana_on_tap` (Crypt Ghast, Vernal Bloom, Wild Growth) is the right *shape* -- a static read inside payment, keyed on what was tapped -- and falls short on BOTH halves of Kinnan's sentence. Its `tapped_permanent` may carry only `types`, `subtypes`, `supertypes` and `attached` (`vocabulary.TAPPED_PERMANENT_KEYS`), `types` is matched as a conjunction (`all(t in tapped.types ...)` in `player_statics.mana_added_on_tap`), and there is no `not_types` and no `any_types`: "a nonland permanent" is unsayable, and enumerating Artifact/Creature/Enchantment/Planeswalker/Battle is neither a legal spelling nor the same set. Its `add_mana` is a **fixed** mana string (or `{"chosen_color_of": "self"}` for Utopia Sprawl) -- `player_statics._mana_added` parses a literal -- so "one mana of any type that permanent produced" cannot be written there either. Any fixed symbol is a different card: a Kinnan that always pays out {G} off a Sol Ring.

(3) A triggered ability on `ability_activated` with `mana_ability: true` -- Forbidden Orchard's spelling, shipped this run -- is legal to write and wrong twice. First, Forbidden Orchard's trigger makes a token: an ordinary triggered ability (603.x) that correctly uses the stack. Kinnan's is a triggered MANA ability (605.1b) and must resolve inside cost payment with no stack and no question, which is exactly why docs/card-dsl.md says of Vorinclex's two halves "neither can be a triggered ability: tapping for mana happens inside payment, where nothing may go on the stack and nothing may stop to ask". Mana that arrives on the stack arrives after the payment it was printed to pay for. Second, docs/card-dsl.md records that the payment solver's own taps emit nothing, so `mana_ability: true` sees only abilities a player activated by hand -- Kinnan would pay out on manual activations and be silent every time the solver tapped his Sol Ring to cast something.

(4) `reflecting` + `any_type` (Reflecting Pool) and `colors_of` (Chrome Mox) are keys on the `add_mana` **op** and answer a different question: what a set of permanents *could* produce, or what colours are printed on a card, polled off the board while planning. Kinnan asks what one permanent *just produced* in this activation, which is not a board fact any selector can name -- and there is no selector for "the permanent whose mana ability is being paid with" in the first place, because at that moment no ability is on the stack to have bound a `subject`.
